editorial:
Set in ancient Alexandria, this film follows Hypatia, a brilliant female philosopher and astronomer who teaches at the famous library. She is surrounded by students who admire her, including her slave Davus, who secretly loves her. As religious tensions rise between pagans, Christians, and Jews, the city becomes a dangerous place. Davus finds himself pulled between his feelings for Hypatia and the promise of freedom if he joins the growing Christian movement. The movie has a serious, thoughtful tone with beautiful visuals of the ancient world.

The acting is strong, especially Rachel Weisz as Hypatia, who brings warmth and intelligence to the role. The sets and costumes look great, and the story tackles big ideas about faith, science, and power. On the downside, the pacing can feel slow at times, and some viewers may find the religious conflict heavy. If you enjoy historical dramas with real depth, this is worth your time. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, a Christian mob attacks Hypatia. They drag her into a church, strip her, and prepare to kill her. Davus, now a Christian, tries to reach her but cannot stop the crowd. To spare her from a worse death, he gives her a drug that puts her to sleep. She is then killed with broken tiles and her body is burned. The film ends on a quiet, tragic note, showing how knowledge and reason were lost to violence and fear.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas with big ideas.
